Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Rowan Novak
Member ID: W128114844
Reference Number: POC-6722E0C945-51497
Date of Notice: 2026-08-17
Requested Service: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Treating Surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated August 17, 2026, Reference Number POC-6722E0C945-51497. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree, and ask that the plan reverse this determination based on the clinical record summarized below.

Summary of relevant clinical findings:

- Symptom duration: Rowan has experienced 14 months of progressive hip pain that is unrelieved by rest.
- Conservative care already completed: 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification (2026-03-27 through 2026-07-03, 24 visits completed), as documented in the physical therapy discharge note; 4 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21 that provided only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- Imaging findings (MRI arthrogram of the hip, 2026-06-16): anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, alpha angle 68 degrees; joint space preserved; Tönnis grade 0.
- Functional limitation: sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting; inability to run or squat.
- Exam: positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain.
- No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

Mapping to the plan's own published coverage rationale:

The only medical policy document I was able to retrieve that appears to correspond to this plan type and procedure code is the UnitedHealthcare Community Plan Medical Policy titled "Surgery of the Hip," Policy Number CS056.AA, effective April 1, 2026. If this is not, in fact, the policy applied to Rowan's Medicaid plan, I ask that the plan identify the correct policy title, number, and effective date in its response to this appeal, and apply the equivalent criteria to the facts below.

That policy defines cam-type impingement, in relevant part, as follows:

"In Cam-type impingement, the femoral head is not round and cannot rotate smoothly inside the acetabulum. A bone spur forms on the edge of the femoral head that grinds the cartilage inside the acetabulum (i.e., radiographic evidence of FAI by imaging includes: the loss of sphericity of the femoral head with resultant bony prominence or alpha angle greater than 50 degrees)."

Rowan's MRI arthrogram documents an alpha angle of 68 degrees, which exceeds this threshold and directly corresponds to the radiographic definition of cam-type FAI set out in the plan's own policy.

The same policy states that hip surgery for FAI is excluded only in specific circumstances:

"Surgical treatment for Femoroacetabular Impingement (FAI) Syndrome is unproven and not medically necessary in the presence of advanced osteoarthritis (i.e., Tönnis Grade 2 or 3) and/or severe cartilage damage (i.e., Outerbridge Grade III or IV)."

Rowan's imaging shows joint space preserved and Tönnis grade 0 — the lowest classification on the scale defined in this same policy, denoting "no signs of osteoarthritis." Because Tönnis grade 0 is not Tönnis grade 2 or 3, and there is no documented Outerbridge grade III or IV cartilage damage in the imaging report, none of the plan's own stated exclusionary criteria for FAI surgery are met. The stated reason for denial — that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity" — is not consistent with the imaging findings actually in the record, which meet the radiographic definition of cam-type FAI and show none of the findings the policy identifies as disqualifying.

I am aware that the plan's coverage rationale also directs reviewers to InterQual® CP: Procedures, "Arthroscopy, Surgical, Hip" criteria for the full medical-necessity checklist. I was not able to obtain the text of those InterQual criteria myself, and I am not quoting or characterizing their specific contents here. However, based on the clinical summary above — 14 months of symptoms, a completed and well-documented course of supervised physical therapy, a 4-month NSAID trial, a corticosteroid injection with only transient relief, positive provocative testing, pain-limited range of motion, and functional impairment (inability to run or squat, pain with sitting and pivoting) — Rowan appears to satisfy the type of symptom-duration, conservative-treatment, and functional-impairment findings that such criteria typically require. I ask that the plan apply the full InterQual criteria to this record and, if any specific element is still considered unmet, identify that element specifically so it can be addressed.

Requested action:

1. Reverse the denial of CPT 29914 (hip arthroscopy with femoroplasty) and approve the requested prior authorization.
2. If the plan relies on a different medical policy or criteria set than the one cited above, please identify that document by title, policy number, and effective date, and provide a copy or citation sufficient for Rowan and Dr. Lindqvist to respond.
3. Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and provide the applicable appeal review timeframe.

This appeal is submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in the notice (due by 2027-02-13).

Please contact me at the phone number or email above, or Dr. Lindqvist's office at [surgeon office phone/fax], with any questions or if additional records are needed.

Sincerely,

Rowan Novak
Member ID: W128114844

Enclosures: Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-27 to 2026-07-03); MRI arthrogram report (2026-06-16); clinic notes documenting NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection (2026-04-21); surgeon's letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist.
